note: A bare message: the standard properties section with to set to queue (005373c00a034040a1057175657565) followed by one data section carrying hi (005375a0026869). The artifact's structure list gives the body as one or more data sections, so one is the minimal body and the two sections in this order are the minimal bare message with properties.

Every section the structure list permits, in the order it lists them: header with durable set (005370c0020141), delivery-annotations with an x-opt key, message-annotations with an x-opt key, properties with to set, one data section, and a footer. The order is the artifact's own diagram, and this vector is what makes an order rule observable at all: with the same six sections in another order it is refused.

The body is one or more data sections, so two are admitted and they are two sections rather than one section carrying both payloads: this is the vector that separates a multi-section body from a fragmented delivery, which belongs to the transfer layer. The second payload is 686f.
The second of the three body choices: one or more amqp-sequence sections, here one carrying two ints.
The third body choice: a single amqp-value section. This is the shape a payload-carried performative arrives in, so the vector is also the one the transaction layer's dispatch rests on.

A zero-octet payload: a message with no sections at all. Reading, recorded rather than cited: the artifact's list gives zero or one of each head and tail section and one of three body choices, and its own diagram draws the bare message box as possibly empty of body sections; peers do send empty transfers, so a payload of no octets is admitted as a message with no sections rather than refused. The reading is what makes the boundary explicit instead of leaving 'no sections' to fall out of a decoder's loop.

The writer's side of the bare message: the sections are written in the order given, and the order is the caller's to preserve because an intermediary MUST NOT reorder, insert or remove a section of the bare message.
